newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom's tinkering seen hurting sales next year.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom's tinkering seen hurting sales next year.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc's efforts to find the right formula for presenting merchandise in its stores could hurt sales at the upscale clothing retailer well into 1997.

Seattle-based Nordstrom this year began moving apparel lines among departments to match the products more closely to the tastes of niche customers. For instance, it moved DKNY women's clothes from "Savvy," which targets so-called progressive shoppers, to "Individualist," which features more contemporary styles.
The short-term result has been confusion among Nordstrom staff and its loyal customers, analysts said.

The shifts have caused a build-up of inventory as shoppers became frustrated at not finding clothes where they once were located, analysts said. Moreover, Nordstrom employees who buy the apparel from manufacturers are on a steep curve when learning about their new target customers.
A relatively solid third-quarter earnings report in November had raised expectations that Nordstrom might have recovered, but a near-term rebound is now considered unlikely.
"I think you could see it within the next six months," said Jennifer Black Groves, an analyst at Portland, Oregon-based Black & Co.

Late Friday, Nordstrom said holiday sales would decline from year-ago levels and cause earnings to fall below analysts estimates. In a statement, Executive Vice President John Goesling attributed the decline "in part" to fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving Day and Christmas this year.
Analysts had expected the company to earn $0.80 a share in its fourth quarter, ending January 31, according to First Call. In the fourth quarter the previous year, Nordstrom earned $0.67 a share.
On Monday, several analysts lowered estimates. Groves cut her fourth-quarter forecast to $0.70 a share.
Still, the excess inventory should be sold and employees trained in the new system by the middle of 1997, putting Nordstrom on track for renewed sales growth, analysts said.
They said a recent launch of clothes from designer Tommy Hilfiger has been a success, and the company was moving to find new designers for some of its private-label clothes.
Also, holiday sales in departments such as men's apparel, shoes and fine jewelry are showing signs of strength.
Lastly, analysts said the snowstorms and freezing rain that blanketed the northwestern United States, where Nordstrom has many stores, held back Christmas sales slightly.
Nordstrom was down 1-3/8 at 36-3/8 in Nasdaq trading late Monday afternoon.
